children: An unprecedented global capex cycle drives the resilient U.S. expansion fueling recent market trends, Deutsche Bank's George Saravelos says in a note. AI and government spending underpin the cycle, which Saravelos says constitutes a rare event. "CapEx booms tend to be sustained, multi-year events," he says, adding that the current capex boom may be one of the largest after World War II reconstruction and it could last for years. However, the dollar has trended weaker through previous capex cycles. "We would not chase the dollar higher after the last few weeks' repricing," Saravelos says. The WSJ Dollar Index falls 0.3%.
